techStack: TypeScript 6.0.2, strict mode (noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch), target ES2023, ESM (type: module)
Express.js 5.2.1 for HTTP server; CORS 2.8.6 middleware
Vitest 4.1.5 with globals enabled; run via `npm test` (or `pnpm --filter benchmark-backend test`)
moduleResolution: bundler; verbatimModuleSyntax: true — imports must use explicit .ts extensions
Package manager: npm; relevant scripts: `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run dev`
features: queryParser.ts currently accepts only camelCase sort values: priceAsc, priceDesc, ratingDesc, nameAsc, nameDesc — checked against VALID_SORT_OPTIONS array
Frontend sends hyphenated sort values (price-asc, price-desc, rating-desc) which currently match nothing — silently dropped, no sort applied
productService.ts response envelope currently returns: { data, count, page, limit, pages }
Tests expect envelope: { data, total, page, limit, totalPages } — count and pages fields cause 18 visible tests to fail
Filters that must not regress: search (case-insensitive name match), category (case-insensitive), inStock (boolean), pagination (page/limit capped at 50)
Sort logic for all five camelCase values already implemented correctly in productService.ts — just unreachable from frontend due to parser mismatch
architecture: Layer order: productRoutes.ts → requireAuth middleware → productController.ts → parseProductQuery (queryParser.ts) → getAllProducts (productService.ts) → fetchAllProducts data
parseProductQuery(raw) in queryParser.ts: validates and coerces raw query params; VALID_SORT_OPTIONS defined at top of file; sort validity check assigns sort only if value is in the array
getAllProducts(query) in productService.ts: chains search → category → inStock filters → sort → pagination; builds and returns envelope object at end of function
productController.ts calls parseProductQuery then getAllProducts and passes result directly to res.json() — no transformation layer; fix must happen in the two target files only
PaginatedResponse<T> interface in types/product.ts already declares fields as total and totalPages — fixing productService aligns runtime output with declared type
edgeCases: Unrecognised sort values after mapping (e.g. ?sort=invalid, ?sort=name-asc): map lookup returns undefined, value remains as-is, validity check rejects it, sort is silently omitted — default order preserved
Backward-compat for camelCase sort values (nameAsc, nameDesc, priceAsc sent directly): these won't match any map key so pass through unchanged; validity check still accepts them — no regression
Mapping must be applied before the VALID_SORT_OPTIONS check, not after, so hyphenated values are translated before they would be rejected
count → total and pages → totalPages rename only affects the productService return statement; no other callers transform these fields before res.json()

TypeScript strict mode: renaming the return object fields in productService must use the correct property names to satisfy the PaginatedResponse<T> type — no separate type file changes needed since the interface already uses total/totalPages
